title: Magic Cube Spectral Analysis — 3D extension of Lo Shu

findings.title: Every layer is a doubly-magic matrix
findings.detail: Each of the 3 horizontal layers has all row sums = 42 AND all column sums = 42. They are full magic squares in their own right, not just cross-sections.

findings.title: ±9 is the 3D spectral invariant (replacing ±2√6 in 2D)
findings.detail: Lo Shu has eigenvalues {M, +2√6, -2√6}. The cube layers have {M, -9, -9}, {M, 0, 0}, {M, +9, +9}. The invariant pair ±9 = ±3² replaces ±2√6 = ±2√(2·3). The degenerate eigenvalue (each non-M eigenvalue appears twice per layer) reflects the extra degree of freedom in 3D.

findings.title: Middle layer is spectrally null — 3D Brahmasthana
findings.detail: Layer 1 (middle) has eigenvalues {42, 0, 0}. After centering (subtract 14), ALL eigenvalues become 0. The middle layer is the spectral center of the cube — the 3D Brahmasthana. This is the volumetric analog of the center cell in Lo Shu.

findings.title: Associative symmetry: c[i,j,k] + c[2-i,2-j,2-k] = 28
findings.detail: Every antipodal pair sums to n³+1 = 28. This is the 3D generalization of the Lo Shu property where opposite cells sum to 10 = n²+1. The cube is fully associative.

findings.title: Centered spectrum: mirror layers with ±9 envelope
findings.detail: After subtracting center value 14, layer eigenvalues become {0,-9,-9}, {0,0,0}, {9,9,0}. Layers 0 and 2 are spectral mirrors. The middle layer vanishes entirely. The non-trivial spectrum lives in the outer shell.

findings.title: Tensor isotropy: σ₁ = 72.75 across all three modes
findings.detail: The first singular value is identical (72.7461) for mode-1, mode-2, and mode-3 unfoldings. The magic cube is spectrally isotropic — no preferred axis. This is a consequence of the row/col/pillar sum constraint.

findings.title: Scaling law: M_cube/M_loshu = (n³+1)/(n²+1)
findings.detail: 42/15 = 2.8 = 28/10 = (n³+1)/(n²+1) for n=3. This is the exact dimensional scaling ratio. Clean algebraic relationship between 2D and 3D magic constants.

comparison_with_yantra_exploration.shared_structure: λ₁ = M (uniform eigenvector = Brahmasthana) in both 2D and 3D
comparison_with_yantra_exploration.3d_center: value 14, spectral weight M=42, middle layer fully null when centered
comparison_with_yantra_exploration.key_difference: 3D introduces eigenvalue degeneracy (multiplicity 2) and a spectrally null middle layer — the extra dimension creates a volumetric void at center rather than a point
